clue.text: Led on tortuous route round dull old building near the cliffs

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters are placed around the synonym for dull
a tortuous route twists about, so the letters of the word led are rearranged

parts.note: an overcast sky is dull and grey

explanation.surface: Someone is led along a winding path around a gloomy old ruin on the clifftops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Led on' reads as the start of a story about a walk, but only 'Led' is fodder. The fortress stands above the white cliffs of Dover on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval fortress at Dover sits high on the famous white chalk cliffs of Kent.

clue.text: Admirable one in front of band waving around?

definitions.text: Admirable one in front of band waving around?

indicators.note: waving around suggests jumbling, so the clue's letters are rearranged
front of picks the opening letter of band

explanation.surface: An admired figure stands before an orchestra, waving his arms about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' takes B from 'band'; 'waving around' rearranges ADMIRABLEONEIN plus B. The whole clue describes the conductor at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Barenboim is a celebrated conductor, who stands before an orchestra waving a baton.

clue.text: Man in depression getting psychiatrist ultimately

parts.note: a vale is a valley, a depression in the land

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the closing letter of psychiatrist

explanation.surface: A depressed man finally goes to see a psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low mood but is a VALE, a valley; 'ultimately' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a manservant, and 'man' is a long-standing word for a gentleman's servant.

clue.text: Joyful Bill perhaps comes in laughing

indicators.note: comes in places the bill word inside the laughing word

parts.note: riant is a literary word for laughing or smiling
an ad is an advertisement, of which a poster or bill is an example

explanation.surface: Cheerful Bill strolls in, laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name, but it is a poster, an AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiant face glows with happiness, so radiant means joyful.

clue.text: Worker chopped vegetable for Venetian merchant

parts.note: a worker ant, the classic crossword worker

indicators.note: chopped says the vegetable word loses its last letter

parts.note: an onion is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A labourer chops vegetables for a merchant in Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' cuts the final N from ONION.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio is the title character of Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Joint going after time? Anno Domini — hard lines!

indicators.note: going after says the joint word follows the time letter

parts.note: a rack is a joint of meat, as rack of lamb
anno domini is a jocular phrase for old age

explanation.surface: A joint is consumed after a while; the year of our Lord brings bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard lines!' looks like the British exclamation for bad luck, but means lines of rail. 'Anno Domini' is humorous slang for advancing age.
explanation.definitionFit: Trackage is a collective word for railway track, steel lines that are literally hard.

clue.text: The Navy, renowned for going off course occasionally

indicators.note: a ship going off course strays, so the letters of the fodder are rearranged

explanation.surface: The famous Navy sometimes strays off its route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off course' rearranges the letters of THE NAVY RENOWNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Every now and then means from time to time, an idiom for occasionally.

clue.text: Pet to hang around under the sun

indicators.note: in a down answer, under puts the loitering word below the sun letter

parts.note: to mooch is to hang around idly

explanation.surface: Someone takes a pet out to loaf around in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' works because this is a down clue: S sits above MOOCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet is to kiss and cuddle, and so is to smooch, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Chap lacking prime bit of meat made nasty fillet

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is removed from the chap word

parts.note: a man is a chap

indicators.note: prime bit of picks the opening letter of meat
nasty means badly made, so the letters of made are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man without the best cut of meat made a horrible fillet steak.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN loses its M (the first letter of 'meat') to give AN; 'nasty' rearranges MADE to ADEM.
explanation.definitionFit: An anadem is a garland or headband, and a fillet is a band worn around the head.

clue.text: Mixed message giving Lib Dem's recent history

definitions.meaning: mixed in the sense of blended together, as of a crowd

definitions.text: message giving Lib Dem's recent history
definitions.meaning: Menzies Campbell, nicknamed Ming, had recently been at the head of the Liberal Democrats, so the word split in two reads as that news

explanation.surface: A muddled communication sums up what has lately happened to the Liberal Democrats.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer after four letters: Sir Menzies 'Ming' Campbell led the Liberal Democrats, a British political party, in 2006-07.
explanation.definitionFit: Things mixed together have been blended or combined, as guests circulating at a party.

clue.text: Milk Tray man in broadcast

indicators.note: something in a broadcast is heard rather than read, so the words are said out loud

parts.note: Tray as written, followed by man meaning a don, a university fellow

explanation.surface: The romantic hero of the Milk Tray chocolate adverts appears on television.
explanation.walkthrough: Milk Tray is a British boxed chocolate brand whose TV adverts featured a daring man in black. Here 'Milk' is the verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk a situation is to exploit it, which is a synonym of the phrasal verb in the grid.

clue.text: Exercise too much in wet weather, as seen by public

parts.note: overt means open and public, not hidden
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: An athlete overdoes the exercise by training in the wet, in full view of the public.
explanation.definitionFit: To train beyond the point of benefit is to exercise excessively, a synonym in verb form.

clue.text: Insect you once caught and fastened with a piece of metal

definitions.text: fastened with a piece of metal

indicators.note: caught says the old pronoun is held within the insect word

parts.note: a ked is a sheep tick, a wingless fly
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: An insect you once trapped was pinned down with a metal clip.
explanation.walkthrough: KED is a crossword regular for the sheep tick; 'once' marks YE as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something locked with a key has been fastened by a small shaped piece of metal.

clue.text: Old boy in house, or one sleeping rough?

indicators.note: in places the old boy abbreviation inside the house abbreviation

parts.note: OB is an abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Is the old man indoors, or out sleeping on the streets?
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp or vagrant with no home is someone who sleeps rough outdoors.

clue.text: Street put in order — man enters very secure place

indicators.note: enters says the man's name goes inside the combined street and tidying words

parts.note: to groom is to tidy or put in order
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A street is tidied up while a man walks into a highly secure vault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in order' looks like an anagram signal, but it is GROOM, to tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongroom is a fortified vault where valuables are kept safe, so a very secure place.

clue.text: Handle document producing legal change?

parts.note: handle is slang for a name, so this reads as the formal paper by which someone legally changes their name

explanation.definitionFit: A deed poll is the legal document used in Britain to change one's name officially.

clue.text: Snake freed accidentally, subsequently caught in road

indicators.note: subsequently says the next part follows the rearranged letters
something done accidentally is jumbled, so the letters of freed are reordered
in places the cricket letter within the road word

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A snake is released by mistake and later captured on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freed' reads as part of the snake story, but it is the fodder the indicator scrambles, and 'road' is a lane rather than a highway.
explanation.definitionFit: The fer-de-lance is a venomous pit viper of Central and South America.

clue.text: Dull environment for current show

indicators.note: an environment surrounds something, so the dull word goes round the current letters

parts.note: to fade is to grow dull
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A dreary setting makes for the latest performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' suggests up-to-date but is electric current, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: A facade is an outward show, a false appearance put on to deceive.

clue.text: A disease exists on account of rodents

parts.note: gout is a disease of the joints
is means exists

explanation.surface: An illness exists because of rodents.
explanation.definitionFit: Agoutis are burrowing rodents of Central and South America, related to guinea pigs.

clue.text: Infection — so is absent from school period

indicators.note: is absent from says the letters of so are removed from school

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Since an infection, a pupil has been off school for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing S and O from SCHOOL leaves CHOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is a serious bacterial infection of the intestine.

clue.text: Deity lacking pizzazz, lacking heart

indicators.note: lacking heart says the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: something banal is dull and unoriginal, lacking pizzazz

explanation.surface: A god is found to have neither flair nor courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking heart' removes the middle N of BANAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Baal was a fertility god worshipped by the ancient Canaanites and Phoenicians.

clue.text: Plastic WC where builders are working, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are as heard when spoken

parts.note: a WC is a loo, and builders work on a site

explanation.surface: A plastic toilet is installed at the building site.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is British for toilet; said out loud, LOO SITE gives the plastic's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucite is a trade name for a clear acrylic plastic.

clue.text: Frank getting rid of daughter's dog, maybe

indicators.note: getting rid of says a letter is taken out of the frank word

parts.note: candid means frank and honest
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone called Frank has his daughter's dog put down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' poses as a name; it means CANDID, which loses one D.
explanation.definitionFit: A canid is any member of the dog family, so a dog is one example; 'maybe' signals that.

clue.text: Soap liniment in bit of surgery by unconventional olde medico

parts.note: an op is an operation, a bit of surgery

indicators.note: unconventional means out of the usual order, so the letters of olde are rearranged

parts.note: a doc is a medico, a doctor

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned doctor applies a soapy rub during an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unconventional' rearranges OLDE to ODEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Opodeldoc was an old soap-based liniment rubbed on sprains and bruises.

clue.text: Resin man extracted from processed melamine

indicators.note: processed says the letters of melamine are worked over and rearranged once man is taken out

explanation.surface: A resin is made by removing a man from processed melamine.
explanation.walkthrough: MELAMINE less the letters of MAN leaves E, L, E, M, I, which 'processed' rearranges; 'extracted from' marks the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and perfumes.

clue.text: Kick someone who fails to complete the course

definitions.meaning: in rugby, a kick taken from the 22-metre line to restart play

definitions.text: someone who fails to complete the course
definitions.meaning: a student who abandons studies before finishing

explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the restart kick from the 22 has this name, and a student who quits is one too.

clue.text: As far as one can see, there's an ocular inflammation?

definitions.text: As far as one can see

definitions.meaning: split after four letters it describes eyes that feel burning, as with inflammation

explanation.surface: The limit of sight is reached because someone's eyes are sore.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer after four letters for the second, playful reading; the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeshot means range of vision, the distance within which something can be seen.

clue.text: Harassment in MI6's HQ?

definitions.meaning: MI6 is Britain's secret intelligence service; split after four letters, the word suggests a base for spies, who are called moles

explanation.surface: Bullying goes on at the headquarters of British intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: A mole is a spy planted in an organisation; MI6 is the UK foreign intelligence agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Molestation means pestering or harassing someone, a close synonym of harassment.
